Recommendation: Set Temporary Access Pass to one-time use (isUsableOnce = true) rather than reusable, to limit its window of exposure to a single onboarding or recovery event. One real trade-off worth knowing about: registering a 'Passkey in Microsoft Authenticator' on a DIFFERENT device than where the user entered the TAP (e.g. TAP entered on a laptop, passkey stored on their phone) requires the phone to independently complete its own sign-in inside the Authenticator app - it does not inherit the laptop's TAP session. A one-time-use TAP already consumed on the laptop leaves nothing for that phone-side step, and Microsoft's Bluetooth-based fallback for this specific case is unavailable whenever FIDO2 attestation is enforced (see PASS001). If cross-device Authenticator-passkey bootstrap is a real onboarding scenario for this tenant, preferred mitigation is same-device Windows Hello for Business or a short-lived multi-use TAP scoped specifically to onboarding. If business continuity still requires it, a temporary attestation exception can be used as a controlled transition: time-box it, exclude admin/high-value users, log registrations created during the window, and re-enable attestation on a fixed date with cleanup review. This does not change the one-time-use recommendation itself for TAP used other than this specific cross-device case.
